data.G: After research closes, compare the measured candidates and any useful combinations without assuming gains add. Use only src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json. Freshly compile and validate every integrated program, then confirm the best valid candidate independently under the official protocol. Keep the fastest independently confirmed program; if no combination improves, retain the best confirmed candidate.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: the measured, correct baseline leaves three useful, distinct avenues to test—source-data reuse, interaction arithmetic, and thread/launch mapping. The supplied AoS kernel performs O(N²) interactions, and each interaction includes square-root/division work; shared-memory staging may reduce repeated source loads. These are hypotheses, not profiled bottlenecks. The baseline is valid and correct, with three reported timing repetitions averaging 0.001845286 s; there are no prior research results or confirmation measurements. The objective is geometric-mean CUDA-event time for N=4096, 8192, and 16384, subject to all stated oracle, tolerance, input, interface, and protocol requirements. CUDA 12.6.3 guidance supports testing shared-memory reuse and explicit rsqrtf use; candidate performance and correctness must still be measured.

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, test shared-memory staging of source positions and mass so target threads reuse source tiles. Keep the baseline interaction arithmetic and one-target-per-thread mapping as much as practical to isolate the memory change. Explore tile size, loading, synchronization, and permitted launch settings in src/launch.json; handle partial tiles and every valid N correctly. Judge only by fresh correctness checks and the official geometric-mean timing protocol.
children.subject: Shared-memory source tiling

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, independently test reducing per-pair arithmetic while retaining direct source loads and baseline target mapping: use the positive target-mass cancellation in acceleration and explicitly evaluate reciprocal-distance-cubed options such as rsqrtf. Preserve the softened distance, update order, exact mass output, and full support for coincident particles and all stated inputs. Require oracle/tolerance validation, including extreme-mass and distributed large-row checks, before comparing official timings.
children.subject: Interaction arithmetic simplification

children.objective: With direct global source loads and baseline interaction arithmetic, investigate target ownership and launch geometry: block size, items_per_block, and one versus multiple output targets per thread/CTA. Respect that items_per_block is not a kernel argument; derive safe, complete output coverage from n and gridDim.x, masking tails without omissions or duplicates for arbitrary sizes and allowed configurations. Measure the configuration changes with correctness checks and the official timing protocol.
children.subject: Target mapping and launch configuration
